items.title: Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Oneonta, New York, December 28, 2005
items.q: Sam Lyra and his partner. Ralph Herman was arranging for the company... Sam, Irving Berman was the other fellow.

ctx.x: And they were heavy to carry around.

That’s right and they were scratchy. But some 78s were not as scratchy as others. My original recording of “Concerto for Doubles,” I’m glad I’m thinking of this, we had a 50 piece orchestra. Manor. M-A-N-O-R. They were on 57th Street just west of Broadway or Eighth Avenue. Sam Lyra and his partner. Ralph Herman was arranging for the company for different singers, and Ralph said, “Why don’t we do something different? Al Gallodoro just performed a ‘Concerto for Doubles’ that Paul Whiteman had written for him. Why…
Yeah. I think I do. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
